 Mumbai, November 13 : Petrol and diesel prices remained unchanged across major Indian cities on Friday, November 13, with oil marketing companies maintaining retail fuel rates. Petrol was priced at Rs 102.12 per litre in Delhi and Rs 111.21 in Mumbai, while diesel retailed at Rs 95.20 and Rs 97.83 per litre, respectively.    
 International crude oil prices were largely steady in early trade on Friday, November 13, but remained on course for a second consecutive weekly decline as US President Donald Trump signalled that Washington would maintain its blockade of Iranian oil shipments and trade. The prospect of prolonged restrictions, rather than renewed large-scale military action, has eased some immediate concerns over supply disruptions, although attacks on shipping and energy infrastructure continue to keep geopolitical risks elevated.   
 Brent crude futures were down 0.3% at $95.5 per barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude declined 0.5% to $88.3 per barrel. For the week, Brent was headed for a 2.4% decline and WTI for a 2.5% fall. This follows steep losses in the previous week, when the benchmarks plunged 16% and 13%, respectively.   
 The latest decline follows US President Donald Trump’s indication that he would continue the blockade on Iranian oil shipments, trade and economic sanctions, even as he suggested that a deal with Tehran was not necessary to end the war. The prospect of avoiding another major escalation has eased some fears of immediate supply disruptions, although the conflict remains unresolved.   
 The geopolitical picture remains fragile. Iran’s military claimed that four oil tankers were hit by explosions in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, an account Reuters said it could not independently verify. Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis also claimed attacks on a pumping station along Saudi Arabia’s East-West oil pipeline, an oil facility in Yanbu and an Aramco building in Riyadh. These developments have kept concerns over the security of crude shipments from the Gulf alive.   
 Adding to the downward pressure, US crude inventories increased by 4.7 million barrels to 414.4 million barrels in the week ended November 6, according to the Energy Information Administration. This was sharply different from expectations of a 1.1-million-barrel drawdown in a Reuters poll, with weaker demand for refined products and higher imports contributing to the build-up. For India, a sustained decline in international crude benchmarks could offer relief on the import bill, inflation and pressure on the rupee.   
 Check the latest petrol and diesel prices in Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad and other major cities.   
 Petrol Prices   
 Petrol prices remained unchanged across major Indian cities and state capitals on Friday, November 13, with oil marketing companies keeping retail rates steady. In New Delhi, petrol was priced at Rs 102.12 per litre, while consumers in Mumbai paid Rs 111.21 per litre and those in Kolkata Rs 113.51 per litre.   
 Among other metropolitan cities, petrol retailed at Rs 107.76 per litre in Chennai and Rs 111.68 per litre in Bengaluru. Hyderabad continued to have one of the highest rates at Rs 116.15 per litre, while Thiruvananthapuram recorded a price of Rs 115.49 per litre.   
 In northern India, petrol was priced at Rs 102.97 per litre in Gurugram, Rs 101.96 in Noida, Rs 101.89 in Lucknow and Rs 101.54 in Chandigarh. Jaipur recorded a retail price of Rs 113.19 per litre.   
 Among other state capitals, petrol sold at Rs 108.97 per litre in Bhubaneswar and Rs 113.37 in Patna. There was no change in petrol prices across any of the cities listed. Retail fuel rates vary between states and cities due to differences in local taxes, including VAT, and transportation costs.   
 Diesel Prices   
 Diesel prices remained unchanged across major Indian cities and state capitals on Friday, November 13, with oil marketing companies keeping retail rates steady. In New Delhi, diesel was priced at Rs 95.20 per litre, while consumers in Mumbai paid Rs 97.83 per litre and those in Kolkata Rs 99.82 per litre.   
 Among other metropolitan cities, diesel retailed at Rs 99.55 per litre in Chennai and Rs 99.56 per litre in Bengaluru. Hyderabad recorded a price of Rs 104.23 per litre, while Thiruvananthapuram had the highest rate among the listed cities at Rs 104.40 per litre.   
 In northern India, diesel was priced at Rs 95.64 per litre in Gurugram, Rs 95.44 in Noida, Rs 95.36 in Lucknow and Rs 89.47 in Chandigarh. Jaipur recorded a retail price of Rs 98.25 per litre.   
 Among other state capitals, diesel sold at Rs 100.68 per litre in Bhubaneswar and Rs 99.36 in Patna. There was no change in diesel prices across any of the cities listed. Retail rates vary across states and cities due to differences in local taxes, including VAT, and transportation costs.
